memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day
that I brought your divisions out of Egypt. Celebrate this day as a lasting
ordinance for the generations to come. In the first month you are to eat bread
made without yeast, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of
the twenty-first day. For seven days no yeast is to be found in your houses. And
anyone, whether foreigner or native-born, who eats anything with yeast in it
must be cut off from the community of Israel. Eat nothing made with yeast.
Wherever you live, you must eat unleavened bread." - Ex 12:17-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats Himself here, and the repetition is deliberate. He wants this fixed
in their memory. But notice one phrase that is easy to skip: "whether foreigner
or native-born."

From the very first Passover, the door was open to outsiders. Anyone who joined
Israel and came under the covenant was held to the same standard and given the
same protection. This is not an afterthought bolted on later. It is here at the
founding moment of the nation.

That tells us something about God's heart. He was never building an exclusive
club. Rahab the Canaanite, Ruth the Moabite, and many others would find their
place among His people. Paul later writes to Gentile believers that they were
once "excluded from citizenship in Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the
promise" but have now been "brought near by the blood of Christ" (Eph 2:12-13).

Brought near by blood. The same principle as this chapter.

If you have ever felt like an outsider to God's people, look at this verse. The
foreigner was welcome at the first Passover, and the door has only opened wider
since.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever felt you do not truly belong among God's people?
2. Who around you feels like an outsider that you could welcome in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your grace has never been for one people only. Thank You
that the blood of Jesus brought me near. Help me to welcome others as You
welcomed me. Amen.
